name: 7 Bridge
description: Seven Bridge (7 Bridge) is a Japanese Rummy game. 2-5 players. 52-card deck. 7 cards each. Special rule: 7s need only 2-card melds (e.g., 7-7 or 6-7 is valid). Single 7 can be played as 1-card meld. Draw from stock (discard pile restricted). Lay off on any meld. Go out by melding all but last card + discard. All-at-once meld = double score.

history.origins: Seven Bridge is a rummy variant played in Japan in which sevens have a special role. It is also known as Mâ Jan Bridge or Seven Rummy. The name Mâ Jan refers to Mah Jong, but the game has no connection to Contract Bridge and is only distantly related to Mah Jong. The rules are credited to Kuromiya Kimihiko and Takerube Nobuaki.
timeline: 20th century: Japanese rummy variant; rules credited to Kuromiya Kimihiko and Takerube Nobuaki.
history.evolution: Not related to Contract Bridge despite name.

setup.deck: 52 cards. A low, K high. 7 each.

rules.objective: Form melds (sets or sequences), lay off on existing melds, and be the first to go out by melding or laying off all cards except one and discarding that final card.
rules.gameplay: Draw from stock (discard pile only if immediately melding). Meld sets (3-4 same rank) or runs (3+ sequential same suit). 7s special: only need 2 cards for meld (7-7 valid set, 6-7 valid run). Single 7 = 1-card meld. Lay off on any player's melds. Discard to end turn. All-at-once go-out = double score.

scoring.description: Winner scores opponents' remaining cards: 7s=20pts, face cards=10pts, others=pip value. All-at-once = doubled.
scoring.winCondition: Meld all cards and discard last card to go out.
